newsitem.title: FRANCE: French airline flights resume, unions meet.
newsitem.headline: French airline flights resume, unions meet.

text.p: State-owned airline Air France Europe resumed flights out of Paris' Orly airport on Sunday as ground staff discussed whether to continue a strike that began on Friday, an airline spokeswoman said.

She said air traffic was normal. The strike over the airline's merger with parent company Air France forced cancellation of many flights on Friday and all flights on Saturday out of Orly, south of Paris, spoiling the Easter holiday weekend for many travellers.
A union spokesman disputed the airline's version and said management chose to cancel Saturday's flights although staff were not on strike.

He said unions were meeting in the morning to discuss their next step. Ground workers are protesting against the unifying of their pay and employment terms with those of parent company Air France in a merger between the two airlines.
The airline said management would discuss union demands next week and delay until May 1st a disputed new working schedule.
Air France Europe pilots and flight crew have called a two-day strike over pay and conditions for next Monday and Tuesday but the company said all flights would take place.
